# Florence 1490 – Physics, optics & astronomy

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Ground lenses** [`lenses`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lenses.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Florence is a centre of spectacle making; convex and concave lenses are sold. Clear glass (cristallo) comes from Murano. Local: Florentine spectacle makers; Murano glassmakers.
- **Spectacles** [`spectacles`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spectacles.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Florentine makers export them by the hundred, graded by the buyer's age. Frames of bone, horn or leather sit on the nose; no side arms. Local: Florentine spectacle makers.
- **Law of refraction, image formation and vision** [`refraction_optics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/refraction_optics.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Perspectiva (Alhazen, Witelo, Pecham) is taught; Ptolemy's refraction tables are known, no sine law. The eye's crystalline lens is held to be the seat of vision. Local: university of Pisa; painters and perspectivists.
- **Camera obscura** [`camera_obscura`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/camera_obscura.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. Known from Alhazen and Pecham for watching eclipses. Nobody puts a lens in the hole or uses it for drawing. Local: Toscanelli's gnomon hole in the dome of the Duomo (1475).
- **Microscope** [`microscope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/microscope.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. A single bead lens (Leeuwenhoek style) can be made by a glassblower; spectacle lenses are too weak. The hard part is forming tiny lenses and good lighting.
- **Telescope (refractor)** [`telescope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/telescope.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Workshops stock weak convex lenses, but strong concave ones are rare and must be ordered. Lens quality limits magnification to about 3-10x. Local: Florentine spectacle makers.
- **Reflecting telescope** [`reflecting_telescope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reflecting_telescope.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Concave burning mirrors and cast metal mirrors exist. Figuring and polishing a high-tin bronze mirror accurately is the bottleneck. Local: bronze founders; mirror makers.
- **Achromatic lens** [`achromatic_lens`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/achromatic_lens.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Needs two glasses of different dispersion; lead glass is made only for imitation gems and enamel, never in clear optical blanks.
- **Spectrum and the nature of colour** [`spectrum_colour`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spectrum_colour.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Colours are held to be white light weakened by darkness (Aristotle). Crystals and glass are known to throw rainbow colours; a prism is easy to have made. Local: Murano glassmakers.
- **Spectral analysis** [`spectroscopy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spectroscopy.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Needs a good prism, a slit and a nearly colourless flame; a spirit lamp with strong aqua vitae serves.
- **Waves - sound and light** [`wave_nature_light_sound`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wave_nature_light_sound.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Vitruvius likens sound to water ripples; string ratios are taught as musica. Light as a wave is unknown. Local: organ builders; lute makers.
- **Finite speed of light** [`speed_of_light`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/speed_of_light.md) — K2, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Aristotle treats illumination as instantaneous. Alhazen argues that light takes time to travel. A measurable astronomical delay requires a telescope and sustained observations.
- **Photography** [`photography`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/photography.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Goldsmiths can dissolve silver in aqua fortis. Fixing is the problem (no hypo; strong brine or ammonia only partly works). Images made by light smell of sorcery. Local: goldsmiths; apothecaries.
- **Lever, pulley, inclined plane (statics)** [`lever_mechanics_statics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lever_mechanics_statics.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Builders work by rule of thumb; the steelyard is everywhere. Theory (pseudo-Aristotle's Mechanica, Jordanus, Archimedes) sits in manuscripts few craftsmen read. Local: Opera del Duomo; Giuliano da Sangallo.
- **Buoyancy and hydrostatics** [`buoyancy_hydrostatics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/buoyancy_hydrostatics.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept high. The crown story is known from Vitruvius; On Floating Bodies exists only in rare Latin manuscripts. Gold is assayed by touchstone and fire, not by density. Local: goldsmiths; the Zecca (mint).
- **Falling bodies and projectiles** [`falling_bodies`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/falling_bodies.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Aristotelian accounts relate speed to weight and the resisting medium. Scholars discuss uniformly accelerated motion. Comparing actual falls would put competing claims to a test.
- **Laws of motion** [`laws_of_motion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/laws_of_motion.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Buridan's impetus is taught: a thrown body carries an impressed force that fades. Rest is the natural state; the heavens obey other rules.
- **Universal gravitation** [`universal_gravitation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_gravitation.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Heavy things seek the centre of the world, which is the Earth. A force acting across empty space sounds like astrology or magic.
- **Strength of materials and scaling** [`strength_of_materials`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/strength_of_materials.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept high. Builders trust proportion rules and scale models, and assume a model's strength carries over to full size. Loading wires and beams to breaking is cheap. Local: Opera del Duomo; Leonardo da Vinci (in Milan).
- **Sundial and water clock** [`sundial_water_clock`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sundial_water_clock.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Italian hours: 24 equal hours counted from sunset, so noon shifts through the year.
- **Mechanical clock (escapement, spring drive)** [`mechanical_clock`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mechanical_clock.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Weight-driven verge-and-foliot tower clocks, reset by sundial, drift a quarter hour a day. Spring-driven chamber clocks are princely luxuries. Local: Lorenzo della Volpaia; Palazzo della Signoria tower clock; Duomo clock (24-hour dial painted by Uccello).
- **Pendulum clock** [`pendulum_clock`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pendulum_clock.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Clockmakers could attempt a pendulum regulator. At small swings its period depends chiefly on length. The escapement must sustain the swing without disturbing it. Local: Lorenzo della Volpaia.
- **Air pressure and the barometer** [`atmospheric_pressure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atmospheric_pressure.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Nature abhors a vacuum (Aristotle); air is thought weightless in its own place. Needs a long sealed glass tube and mercury, which apothecaries sell. Local: apothecaries (mercury); Murano glassmakers; mining and well engineers. Elsewhere: Almaden (Spain) mercury mines; Idrija, mercury found c. 1490.
- **Air pump and vacuum experiments** [`air_pump_vacuum`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/air_pump_vacuum.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. A void is impossible for Aristotelians. Needs a tightly fitted bronze syringe with leather packing and valves, plus thick glass vessels. Local: bronze founders; Murano glassmakers.
- **Thermometer and temperature scale** [`thermometer_temperature`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/thermometer_temperature.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Physicians judge fever by touch and pulse; Galenic pharmacy counts four degrees of hot and cold. A sealed spirit tube is glassblower's work. Local: Murano glassmakers; apothecaries (aqua vitae).
- **Specific and latent heat** [`latent_specific_heat`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/latent_specific_heat.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Heat and cold are qualities, not quantities. Needs a thermometer first.
- **Heat as motion, conservation of energy, limits of engines** [`heat_energy_conservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heat_energy_conservation.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Engineers seriously draw perpetual-motion wheels and self-driving mills. Heat is the element fire.
- **Weather instruments and forecasting** [`weather_instruments`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/weather_instruments.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Alberti described a wind-pressure plate. Cusanus proposed balancing dry wool against a fixed weight to follow changes in humidity.
- **Spherical Earth and its size** [`round_earth_size`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/round_earth_size.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Learned geography treats Earth as spherical. Estimates of its circumference and of Asia's eastward extent differ, with large consequences for a westward voyage. Local: Toscanelli's papers and pupils; Berlinghieri's printed Ptolemy (Florence 1482).
- **Cause of the seasons (tilted axis)** [`seasons_axial_tilt`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/seasons_axial_tilt.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Taught correctly as the obliquity of the Sun's path (Sacrobosco), but with the Sun circling a fixed Earth. Local: Toscanelli's gnomon in the Duomo.
- **Cause and prediction of eclipses** [`eclipse_prediction`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/eclipse_prediction.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Causes are understood. Predictions from the Alfonsine Tables and Regiomontanus' printed Ephemerides can be off by an hour or more. Local: astrologers; university of Pisa. Elsewhere: Nuremberg, Regiomontanus' successors (Bernhard Walther).
- **Heliocentric model** [`heliocentrism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heliocentrism.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Aristarchus is known to a few humanists through Archimedes and Plutarch. Copernicus, aged 17, enters Krakow university in 1491. Absurd rather than heretical in 1490.
- **Kepler's laws of planetary motion** [`keplers_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/keplers_laws.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Astronomers have planetary tables, but testing elliptical orbits needs long, accurate observations and extensive calculation. A drawn ellipse alone would establish little.
- **Distances of Moon, Sun and stars (parallax)** [`astronomical_distances`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/astronomical_distances.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Ptolemy's lunar distance is fairly close. His solar distance is about twenty times too small. The fixed stars belong to a sphere beyond Saturn.
- **Comets as orbiting bodies** [`comets_orbits`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/comets_orbits.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Comets are fiery vapours below the Moon and omens of deaths and wars. Toscanelli recorded positions of several, including the comet of 1456.
- **Tides caused by Moon and Sun** [`tides`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tides.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The link to the Moon is accepted and explained astrologically. Tuscan tides are too small to matter; Venice and the Atlantic ports care. Elsewhere: Venice; Atlantic ports of Portugal and Flanders.
- **The Earth as a magnet** [`terrestrial_magnetism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/terrestrial_magnetism.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The needle is thought to seek the Pole Star or a magnetic mountain. Peregrinus' letter on the magnet circulates in manuscript. Local: Elba lodestone (Monte Calamita). Elsewhere: Nuremberg compass-sundial makers mark the needle's deviation.
- **Deep time - age of the Earth, strata and fossils** [`deep_time_geology`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/deep_time_geology.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Biblical chronologies count thousands of years. Tuscan shell beds offer evidence of former seas, although scholars differ over how shells came to lie inland.
